March 31st, 1920. 191
REPORT ON Inquiries re Articles in "Shanghai Times" on
Bolshevik Propaganda in China.
Made by D. I. Givens Forwarded by Chief Detective Officer.
Sir,
I have interviewed the writer of the articles
entitled "
in the "Shanghai Times" of Bolshevik Propaganda in
China". He is a Swiss subject named Joseph Hofer, who
has passed 12 years in Russia. Mr. Hofer's father was
killed by the Bolshevika, and he himself narrowly
escaped being murdered by the same party on two occasions.
He is consequently very intolerant of Bolshevism, and
probably has allowed his feelings to sway him to some
extent in his writings. His story that "there is something
in a certain place outside the Settlement" is based
on a report made to him by a Russian assistant, who
stated that he kept watch for several days outside
the offices of the Russian newspaper "Shanghai Life".
On one occasion he saw two men leave that address in
a motor car and another time saw same pair go away
from there on bicycles. He followed them on the latter
occasion into Chapei. On reaching the Russian Church
they threatened him with revolvers, and he was forced
to give up the pursuit.
Mr. Hofer, who lives at No. 17A Range Road, states
that there are several Jews living in a boarding-house
who
at No. 77 Broadway Terrace openly boast of their
Bolshevist sentiments at table.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
D. I.
C. D. O.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY,. MARCH 23, 1920.
BOLSHEVIK PROPAGANDA IN CHINA
Agents At Work In Shanghai: In Touch With Disgruntled
Politicians And Student Body In French Concession
A MAD DREAM OF WORLD CONQUEST
(Continued From Yesterday.)

There is another interesting docu-
ment in existence which shows that
Trotzky, besides receiving a salary
of Roubles 30,000 per month, is
rapidly amassing a huge fortune. It
is common knowledge that he has
sent out to a bank in Argentine
several million roubles in gold.
When taxed by Lenin, Trotzky is
said to have replied that he realises
that the movement in Russia will
fade away as rapidly as it had
broken out, therefore he was going
to make as much out of the
"chance" as he could. These are
the men that are intriguing for
power in the Far East.
Campaign Opened in Earnest
There is overwhelming evidence
that the Bolsheviks have opened
their campaign in China in earnest.
Many of their agents are staying in
hotels in Hongkew and the French
Concession. There is one man, who,
we have every reason to believe, is
directing the propaganda work in
Shanghai, who lives in the French
Concession. Of late he has been
visited by several Chinese, some of
them representing a student body,
and one at least coming from a man
who once was very popular, in fact a
hero, in the eyes of the Chinese
people. The callers in short, repre-
sent certain people who imagine
they have a grievance against the
central government or against the
local Municipal Administration. It
would seem, therefore, that the
Bolsheviks are making a bid for the
doubtful support of these malcon-
tents. The Bolsheviks, who are
past masters in the art of lying, will
experience no difficulty in playing
upon the feelings of these "water-
brained" intriguers. Another fre-
quent caller is a man who is con-
nected with a local labour organisa-
tion.
This Russian who is attracting like
a magnet the notorious disgruntled
politicians in Shanghai, is evidently
recruiting workers for the Bolshe-
vik cause. There is a report that a
printing plant has been established
outside the Settlement which will
turn out all the literature needed in
the campaign in Shanghai. We have
made exhaustive enquiries into the
location of the plant, and unfortun-
ately report that though we have been
able, up to the present, to get no
indications are not wanting that
there is something in a certain place
just beyond the Settlement that is
drawing numbers of Russians at all
hours of the day and night. The
men directing the plant, or whatever
it may be, live in that road
and one of them travels to the place
daily on a bicycle. It is said that he
always goes out armed with a re-
volver.
Where Work Will First Start
The question has been frequently
heard: Will the Bolsheviks succeed
in winning the Chinese people over
to their doctrine? They will not
start their work among the intelli-
gent and thinking classes, with
whom they will find short shrift,
unless, of course, these men are
nursing grievances, imaginary or
otherwise, against the Peking or the
local Government. In that case
the Bolsheviks will find the assist-
ance which these men are able to
render of great value. Where the
Bolsheviks will first start their pro-
paganda will be amongst coolies and
the poor class of people who are
mostly illiterate and ignorant. These
are the people who will lend a will-
ing ear to what the Bolsheviks will
have to say. They become easy
converts to Bolshevism.
Many Russians, who are believed
to be agents of the Bolsheviks,
can speak the Chinese language
quite fluently. A number learnt the
language through long residence in
North China, others are the output
of a school said to have been financ-
ed by the Bolsheviks at Harbin.
There is a Russian journal here in
Shanghai which has been exhibiting
obvious pro-Bolshevik tendencies.
In attempting to throw dust in the
eyes of the Chinese Government, it
one day declared that the Govern-

ment need not be anxious to take measures against a Bolshevik invasion, in fact, there was no necessity, it said.

A Celebration Stopped
The other day the local Bolsheviks wanted to celebrate by demonstration the anniversary of the revolution in Russia. But the ever watchful local authorities stepped in and put a stop to it. It was a wise decision, for had the Bolsheviks been allowed to do as they pleased, they would have said to the Chinese people: "See how powerful we are! We do as we please. It proves to you that our doctrine is a just one, otherwise think you the local authorities would have permitted us to hold our little demonstration?"

Creating An Impression
In this connection the following telegram sent out by Reuter's Agency, and published in our issue yesterday, is illuminating:--
With reference to the Moscow wireless report of disaffection among the Japanese troops in Siberia the War Office states that the report is an entire fabrication and that this and similar reports which have recently been circulated in China and elsewhere are evidently Bolshevik propaganda aiming at creating the impression that the Reds are gaining strength in the Far East.
The Bolsheviks are agitating for a world revolution, and have not hesitated in the course of their work to sacrifice a great country, which has run red with innocent blood.
If China will but take precautionary measures, she will not find it difficult to frustrate the Bolsheviks evil plans. The first essential antidote to their propaganda is a good government, for where there is a good government, the Bolsheviks will find powerful adherents to their cause. The main thing is the settlement of the dispute between the North and the South, thereby removing one very fruitful field, which

it is to be feared, will prove very susceptible to Bolshevik influence.
Time Opportune For Counter Move
It would seem then that the moment has now arrived for a campaign of anti-Bolshevik propaganda in China to be begun. Much good work could be done by way of instructing the students and, through them to reach the people. A full exposition of what the Bolsheviks have done in Russia and Siberia will open the eyes of the people to the danger facing them to-day. Above all, public opinion in Shanghai should be aroused to such a pitch that a strong demand should be made to the local authorities to institute greater discrimination in permitting the landing of Russians in Shanghai. In this manner, it is hoped to eradicate, or, at least, check, the influx of the more undesirable characters.

Mad Dream Of World Conquest
The Bolsheviks failed miserably in their propaganda in England and France. Bela Kun, in Hungary, who for a time was successful, did no better. They are now looking towards the Far East. "It is there," exclaimed Lenin, "that we shall deliver a smashing blow to England and France. There we will set alight the fire of Bolshevism, and the red glow shall illuminate the whole world. There we will create an army with which we shall conquer Europe and America."
It is big game, if the plans of the Bolsheviks are to be taken seriously, but whatever opinion one may care to express in regard to this latter phase of Bolshevik propaganda, there can be no manner of doubt whatever that China, should she fall into the hands of the Bolsheviks, will suffer terribly. As a stepping stone to the realisation of their mad dream of world conquest, China will have a heavy burden to bear.
And the Bolsheviks are now in her midst, in Shanghai, carrying out the preliminary plans of their campaign.

CENTRAL POLICE Station.
April 7th 1920. 191

REPORT ON Alleged Plans Against Consul General for Russia.

Made by D. I. Givers Forwarded by Chief Detective Officer.

Sir,
J. Hofer, a Swiss, who acts as Russian correspondent
for the Shanghai Times, and who lives at No. 17A Range
Road, reports that he overheard a conversation between
a Russian named Gourman, who lives in that address and
Semeschko on the evening of April 3rd. Gourman and
Semeschko were speaking about giving a lesson to "old
Grosse", and Semeschko suggested energetic action. Gourman
said he knew some fellows capable of administering the
blow, and that he would speak further about it the following
day.

I called at the Russian Consulate on the afternoon
of 7th instant and, in the absence of Mr. Grosse, reported
the above matter to Mr. Ivanoff, Vice Consul.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
D. I.

C. D. O.
